notes: Budgets for scripts/perf/dcperf.py. A gated metric fails the check when it is over budget * (1 + tolerance) or was not measured.
linux-per-user is seeded from the RHEL 9.8 per-user column of the 1.0.6 performance baseline (~/dc-eh/plans/r107/data/PERF-BASELINE.md, dc-rhel, 4 vCPU). Each entry names its source row.
gate false: reported next to its budget but not gated, with the reason in why (max is a single-sample tail; burst latency depends on the runner CPU).

hook.claudecode.burst.p50_ms.why: not gated: burst latency is CPU-bound (32 hook shells on 4 vCPUs) and GitHub runners vary in CPU. CI run 41255145781 on ubuntu-latest: claudecode burst p50 774 / p95 1074 ms. Same harness on the build box pinned to 4 CPUs (taskset): rc23 710e2cc0d8 p50 477-502 / p95 680-746 ms, 1.0.7 tip 94d60a0462 p50 457-465 / p95 652-685 ms, so no regression. Gate it once dcperf has run on dc-rhel (rel-1-0-6:GAP-0239 sweep recipe); not_allowed stays gated.

cli.skill_scan.p50_ms.why: not gated: single-thread CPU-bound and CI runner CPUs differ: 4953, 7514 and 8446 ms on three ubuntu-latest runs of this branch (CI 41255145781, 41257204077, 41258641067; within 1% across the 3 scans of each run; AMD EPYC 7763 on the slowest), 5874-6074 ms on the build box. Gate it once results are normalized by host.cpu_score_ms against the dc-rhel score (rel-1-0-6:GAP-0239 sweep recipe).
